_comment: Rule table for analysis/triage.py. Reviewable without touching code. Names are PFIDB-exact (the classifier's own namespace), which is why name matching is safe here: a report can only emit names from this namespace. Do NOT add colloquial names - 'Junin virus' would never match; the DB files it as 'Argentinian mammarenavirus'.

thresholds._escalation_host_share_why: Co-location alone was enough to escalate a watchlist organism to CONFIRM: the gene was in the sample and the genus was A documented host. That let Serratia marcescens (WBM185) escalate on a CTX-M whose host pool it holds 1.3% of - 77 organisms could carry it and Serratia was one of the smallest. Escalation now also requires the organism to be the MOST ABUNDANT documented host in the sample, or to hold at least this share of the pool. Below that, naming it is arbitrary among the candidates. Set 2026-08-12; A. baumannii in WBM232 holds 21% AND tops its pool, so the one operationally significant finding in the batch is unaffected.

Bacillus anthracis.amr_expectation: Chromosomal bla1/bla2 beta-lactamases are present but poorly expressed; wild-type B. anthracis remains penicillin-susceptible and carries no recognised mobile resistome. An acquired resistance gene in this genus would itself be the finding.

Yersinia pestis.amr_expectation: Wild-type Y. pestis is susceptible to all first-line agents. The two documented multi-resistant isolates (Madagascar, 1995) carried IncP plasmids and are the exception that defines the rule; no endemic mobile resistome exists.

Francisella tularensis.amr_expectation: Intrinsically resistant to beta-lactams via a chromosomal class A beta-lactamase, but with no acquired mobile resistome; clinical resistance to aminoglycosides, tetracyclines or fluoroquinolones has essentially not been reported.

Brucella melitensis.amr_expectation: Brucella spp. have no documented mobile resistome; rifampicin and fluoroquinolone resistance, when reported, is chromosomal point mutation (rpoB, gyrA). A MEGARes acquired-gene hit is not expected to belong to this organism.

Brucella abortus.amr_expectation: See Brucella melitensis: no documented mobile resistome; resistance when reported is chromosomal point mutation.

Brucella suis.amr_expectation: See Brucella melitensis: no documented mobile resistome; resistance when reported is chromosomal point mutation.

Burkholderia mallei.amr_expectation: See Burkholderia pseudomallei: intrinsic chromosomal PenA and AmrAB-OprA, no acquired mobile resistome.

Burkholderia pseudomallei.amr_expectation: Resistance is intrinsic and chromosomal - the PenA beta-lactamase and the AmrAB-OprA efflux pump - not acquired. Ceftazidime resistance arises by penA mutation or amplification, which read-level MEGARes calling cannot see.

Chlamydia psittaci.amr_expectation: Obligate intracellular with a reduced genome; no mobile resistome is described, and laboratory tetracycline resistance has not been reproduced clinically.

Coxiella burnetii.amr_expectation: Obligate intracellular; not routinely cultured for susceptibility testing. Doxycycline resistance is attributed to chromosomal mutation, and no mobile resistome is described.

Rickettsia prowazekii.amr_expectation: Obligate intracellular with a heavily reduced genome; no acquired resistance genes are described in the genus.

Salmonella enterica.subspecies_required: serovar (Typhi / Paratyphi / Typhimurium) - PFIDB carries no serovar rank (1 of 27,827 entries has subsp./serovar/str.), so a laboratory strain and a notifiable one are indistinguishable here

_taxonomy_notes_comment: Species whose name misleads. Emitted alongside any call.

taxonomy_notes.Brucella anthropi: Formerly Ochrobactrum anthropi, moved into Brucella in 2020. Ubiquitous reagent contaminant, NOT zoonotic brucellosis. Not a CDC agent.
taxonomy_notes.Bacillus cereus: B. anthracis near-neighbour. Chromosome is ~99% identical; only pXO1/pXO2 separate them.
taxonomy_notes.Staphylococcus argenteus: Formerly part of S. aureus. Cross-maps with S. aureus reads.

_kitome_comment: Seed list of reagent/kit contaminant genera (Salter 2014, Eisenhofer 2019). The computed cross-sample enrichment test is the primary filter; this list only lowers confidence further.
_amr_comment: MEGARes Group -> how to read it. class: acquired | intrinsic | core_essential | regulator | point_mutation | rrna_conserved | efflux_ubiquitous. Only 'acquired' can raise a tier on its own.

MECA.note: Methicillin resistance. Needs a host organism to be meaningful; requires mecR1/mecI context and culture confirmation.
MECA.high_consequence_basis: Methicillin resistance changes first-line therapy for any staphylococcal infection.

CTX.note: CTX-M extended-spectrum beta-lactamase. Genuinely acquired, plasmid-borne.
CTX.high_consequence_basis: CTX-M ESBL removes third-generation cephalosporins from the options.

BLAZ.note: Staphylococcal penicillinase. Near-universal in staphylococci since the 1950s; expected background, not a finding.

TETK.note: Tetracycline MFS efflux, plasmid-borne in staphylococci.

FOSA.note: Fosfomycin thiol transferase; intrinsic in many Gram-negatives.

FOLP.note: Sulfonamide resistance requires specific dihydropteroate synthase substitutions.

ICR.note: Colistin phosphoethanolamine transferase (mcr-like). Verify allele before reporting.

ADEJ.note: AdeIJK RND efflux pump. Chromosomal and present in essentially every A. baumannii. Resistance requires OVEREXPRESSION (adeN repressor mutation), which DNA presence cannot measure.

LPXA.note: First Raetz enzyme of lipid A biosynthesis. A core essential gene in every Gram-negative; presence is the default state, not a resistance signal. Colistin resistance needs a LOSS-OF-FUNCTION variant, which needs depth to call.

MECI.note: Repressor of mecA. Meaningless without mecA - its only function is to switch mecA off. Homologous to blaI and filed under the same MEGARes mechanism, so it cross-maps from a bla operon.

BLAR.note: blaR1 sensor-transducer of the bla operon.

GYRA.note: Fluoroquinolone resistance requires QRDR substitutions. Gene presence is universal - every bacterium has gyrA.

PARC.note: As GYRA - topoisomerase IV is universal.

RPOB.note: Rifampicin resistance requires RRDR substitutions. rpoB is universal and essential.

FUSA.note: Fusidic acid resistance requires EF-G substitutions. fusA is universal and essential.

A16S.note: 16S rRNA is present in every bacterium and highly conserved, so reads from the whole community pile onto it. Not a resistance call.

MLS23S.note: 23S rRNA is universal and conserved. Not a resistance call without variant evidence.

NORA.note: Chromosomal MFS efflux, ubiquitous in staphylococci. Expression-dependent.

QACAB.note: Biocide efflux. Relevant to disinfectant tolerance, not antibiotic therapy.

MGRA.note: Global staphylococcal regulator, not a resistance determinant by itself.

CADD.note: Metal resistance, environmental. Not clinically actionable.

COPB.note: Copper resistance protein. Environmental//metal tolerance, not an antibiotic determinant.

PCOC.note: Plasmid-borne copper resistance. Environmental, but plasmid-borne - note co-selection potential.

MERT.note: Mercury transport protein (mer operon). Environmental. mer operons ride on Tn21-family transposons that also carry class 1 integrons, so presence hints at mobile-element load.

MERP.note: Periplasmic mercury binding protein (mer operon). Environmental; see MERT on co-selection.

CADC.note: Cadmium resistance regulator. Environmental; common on staphylococcal plasmids.

SILP.note: Silver RND efflux. Environmental/biocide. Relevant to silver-impregnated surfaces, not to therapy.

EEFX.note: Acid resistance protein. Stress tolerance, not an antimicrobial resistance determinant.

SODB.note: Superoxide dismutase. Housekeeping oxidative-stress enzyme present in nearly all bacteria; presence is the default state.

QACG.note: qacG SMR biocide efflux, staphylococcal plasmid-borne. Disinfectant tolerance, not antibiotic resistance.

AAC6-PRIME.note: aac(6') aminoglycoside acetyltransferase. Acquired in most organisms, BUT aac(6')-Ig/-Im are chromosomal and intrinsic in several Acinetobacter species - check the host before reporting.

ANT3-DPRIME.note: ant(3'')-Ia / aadA streptomycin-spectinomycin adenylyltransferase. Classic class 1 integron gene cassette - its presence with QACEDELTA1 indicates an integron.

APH6.note: aph(6)-Id / strB streptomycin phosphotransferase. Transposon-borne, usually paired with aph(3'')-Ib.

ERM.note: erm 23S rRNA methyltransferase - macrolide/lincosamide/streptogramin B resistance.

VGA.note: vga ABC-F protein - streptogramin A, lincosamide and pleuromutilin resistance. Plasmid-borne in staphylococci.

MUPA.note: mupA - a second, plasmid-borne isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase conferring HIGH-LEVEL mupirocin resistance. Clinically important: mupirocin is the standard nasal decolonisation agent for MRSA carriage, so mupA predicts decolonisation failure.
MUPA.high_consequence_basis: Mupirocin IS the standard decolonisation agent, so high-level mupA resistance means the first-line response to a staphylococcal finding would silently fail. An operational decision changed by the result is the test for this flag.

CMX.note: cmx phenicol MFS efflux. Common in Corynebacterium and other actinobacteria, often on mobile elements.

SULII.note: sul2 sulfonamide-resistant dihydropteroate synthase. Plasmid-borne; sul genes are among the most reliable acquired-resistance markers.

DFRC.note: dfrC trimethoprim-resistant dihydrofolate reductase. Staphylococcal, plasmid-borne.

TET39.note: tet(39) tetracycline MFS efflux. Plasmid-borne, characteristic of Acinetobacter.

TETL.note: tet(L) tetracycline MFS efflux. Plasmid-borne in Gram-positives.

BLAA.note: Class A beta-lactamase. Acquired; identify the specific family before reporting a spectrum.

CARB.note: CARB/PSE-family carbenicillin-hydrolysing class A beta-lactamase. Acquired.

QACEDELTA1.note: qacE-delta-1 - a TRUNCATED biocide efflux gene that forms the 3'-conserved segment of CLASS 1 INTEGRONS. Its real value is as an integron marker: where it appears, expect co-mobilised resistance cassettes (see ANT3-DPRIME, SULII).

RPOCL.note: Daptomycin resistance requires rpoC substitutions. rpoC is universal and essential; presence means nothing on its own.

FABI.note: Enoyl-ACP reductase - the triclosan target. Essential fatty-acid synthesis gene present in nearly all bacteria; resistance requires substitutions, not presence.

ABAF.note: AbaF fosfomycin MFS efflux. Chromosomal and intrinsic in Acinetobacter baumannii.

ABAQ.note: AbaQ MFS efflux. Chromosomal and intrinsic in A. baumannii.

ABUO.note: AbuO multi-biocide RND efflux. Chromosomal and intrinsic in A. baumannii.

AMVA.note: AmvA MFS efflux. Chromosomal and intrinsic in A. baumannii.

FOSB.note: fosB fosfomycin thiol transferase. Chromosomal and intrinsic in staphylococci and Bacillus.

ADEG.note: AdeFGH RND efflux pump component. Chromosomal in A. baumannii; resistance requires OVEREXPRESSION, not presence.

ADEH.note: AdeFGH RND efflux pump component. Chromosomal in A. baumannii; see ADEG.

ADET1.note: AdeT RND efflux pump component. Chromosomal in A. baumannii.

ADET2.note: AdeT RND efflux pump component. Chromosomal in A. baumannii.

MEXE.note: MexEF-OprN RND efflux component. Chromosomal in Pseudomonas; expression-dependent.

TETR.note: TetR repressor of tet(A). Without tet(A) in the same sample there is nothing for it to regulate.

ADEN.note: AdeN, TetR-family repressor of the AdeIJK efflux pump. THIS IS THE GENE THAT MATTERS: AdeIJK presence is intrinsic and uninformative, but LOSS-OF-FUNCTION in adeN de-represses AdeIJK and IS the resistance mechanism. Presence at good breadth and depth does not prove overexpression - it identifies the target for variant calling, which needs deeper coverage than this assay provides.

ADEL.note: AdeL, LysR-family regulator of AdeFGH. Loss-of-function de-represses AdeFGH and causes the resistance; presence alone does not.

ADES.note: AdeS sensor kinase of the AdeRS two-component system regulating AdeABC. Gain-of-function substitutions drive AdeABC overexpression; presence alone does not.

MEXT.note: MexT, LysR-family activator of MexEF-OprN. Variant alleles drive overexpression; presence alone does not.

RLMH.note: RlmH is a housekeeping 23S rRNA methyltransferase (m3-pseudouridine, helix 89), not a resistance methylase. MEGARes files it under the same mechanism string as erm, which is why the mechanism map alone gets it wrong.

FOSX.note: fosX is chromosomal and intrinsic in Listeria monocytogenes and several other Gram-positives; presence is the default state for those hosts.

CRPP.note: crpP is chromosomal in Pseudomonas aeruginosa; plasmid-borne variants exist but chromosomal is the default.

_marker_comment: Virulence/plasmid markers searched in the VFDB table. Absence downgrades the parent agent.  Two kinds: `markers` are two-way (present=ESCALATE, absent=downgrade to NO_ACTION) and are only used where the gene is unique to the agent and reliably in VFDB. `supporting_markers` are ONE-WAY (present=ESCALATE, absent=no change) for agents where VFDB coverage cannot be certified from the report, so a miss must never read as an exclusion. All searches are restricted to VFDB rows whose reference strain shares the taxon genus.

class_thresholds._comment: Per-class gene thresholds. breadth/depth = full-length route. partial_breadth/partial_depth = fragment route, requires higher depth. A group entry in group_thresholds overrides its class.

long_read_thresholds._comment: Platform override applied when mean read length >= long_read_length_bp. A 6-8 kb read spans a 1 kb gene end to end, so breadth saturates near 100% and the 80% gate stops discriminating - hence the higher breadth. One unit of depth is one whole molecule rather than a thin pileup of 150 bp fragments, so the depth gate comes down. Two molecules, not one: long-read basecall accuracy (Q10-13 in this batch) cannot settle an allele from a single read.

acquired.why: Full length = >=95% of the reference at >=2x, i.e. at least two spanning molecules. Fragment route = >=80% at >=5x.

group_thresholds._comment: Overrides for groups where the class default is wrong. Each entry states WHY, so the threshold can be argued with rather than merely obeyed.

CTX.why: CTX-M is an ESBL - a clinically decisive acquired gene, and the CTX-M family is diverse enough that reads from one allele cover a reference allele partially. Missing a real ESBL costs more than over-calling one, so the fragment route is relaxed to 8x. Report as partial: the family is established, the allele is not.

MECA.why: Same argument as CTX: methicillin resistance is decisive, and a partial mecA still warrants culture.

BLAZ.why: Staphylococcal penicillinase is near-universal background. Raised, and the fragment route disabled, so it does not crowd out real findings.

mechanism_classes._comment: Fallback classification by MEGARes (Type, Mechanism), keyed 'Type|Mechanism'. Resolution order is group override -> this map -> keyword fallback in code. 115 entries cover 397 distinct groups, and generalise to groups never seen.

amr_host_hints._comment: Host-range hints for the HTML report ONLY. MEGARes carries no organism column, so these are literature expectations about which organisms typically carry a gene family - NOT evidence from this dataset, and never an input to any verdict. The report renders them as INFERRED and repeats that assembly could not attribute these genes (docs/biothreat_assessment.md 2.5). A hint is shown only when a matching organism is independently present in the same sample. Genus lists were extended 2026-08 for organisms on the CDC/WHO lists that had no coverage: Shigella (genomically Escherichia coli, same plasmid- and integron-borne resistome), Morganella and Providencia (Morganellaceae, same acquired Enterobacterales repertoire), Vibrio on the SXT/R391 ICE cargo genes only (sul2, floR, strAB, aadA, tetA - Jia 2026, doi:10.3389/fmicb.2026.1751786), and Campylobacter on erm(B) and aph(3')-III (Katic 2026, doi:10.1089/fpd.2024.0173). Mycobacteroides was added alongside Mycobacterium after the 2018 genus split, because the report now names the organism Mycobacteroides abscessus. 2026-08-12: added the Ade* RND efflux families (AdeABC/AdeFGH/AdeIJK and regulators) for Acinetobacter. These were the gap that mattered: an INTRINSIC gene is definitionally attributable to its own genus, which makes it the strongest attribution case in the file, and it was the only one uncurated. LpxA deliberately NOT added - lipid A biosynthesis is universal among Gram-negatives, so its presence attributes to nothing and confers no resistance without a mutation the report cannot see.

clinical_watchlist._comment: Clinically serious organisms that are NOT CDC bioterrorism agents. Built because the threat_list is exclusively CDC A/B/C, so A. baumannii - the most operationally important organism in this project - could never exceed MONITOR. Sources: WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List and the ESKAPE group. CEILING IS 'CONFIRM', NEVER 'ESCALATE': escalation stays reserved for a CDC threat agent with its confirmatory marker. A watchlist organism reaches CONFIRM only when it is enriched in this sample AND an acquired resistance gene of a listed class is present in the same sample and this genus is one of its documented hosts. That is CO-LOCATION, NOT CO-ATTRIBUTION - MEGARes has no organism column (docs/biothreat_assessment.md 2.5) - and CONFIRM means 'culture with AST', which is the correct action either way.

Acinetobacter baumannii.note: Carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii is WHO critical priority and a leading cause of hospital outbreaks. Lipopeptide genes are listed because colistin is the last-line agent.

Pseudomonas aeruginosa.note: Carbapenem-resistant P. aeruginosa, WHO critical priority.

Klebsiella pneumoniae.note: Carbapenem- and ESBL-producing Enterobacterales, WHO critical priority.

Enterobacter cloacae.note: ESKAPE Enterobacterales, AmpC and carbapenemase host.

Enterococcus faecium.note: Vancomycin-resistant E. faecium, WHO high priority. Glycopeptide genes are the escalating signal; note aac(6')-Ii is INTRINSIC in this species and must not be read as acquired.

Enterococcus faecalis.note: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci. Same aac(6') intrinsic caveat as E. faecium.

Stenotrophomonas maltophilia.note: Intrinsically multi-resistant opportunist; co-trimoxazole is the mainstay, so sulfonamide genes matter.

Streptococcus pneumoniae.note: Penicillin-non-susceptible S. pneumoniae, WHO medium priority.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae.note: Third-generation cephalosporin-resistant N. gonorrhoeae, WHO high priority.

Helicobacter pylori.note: Clarithromycin-resistant H. pylori, WHO high priority.
Helicobacter pylori.amr_expectation: Clinically important resistance in H. pylori is point-mutational, not acquired: 23S rRNA for clarithromycin, gyrA for levofloxacin, rdxA for metronidazole (Matei 2026, doi:10.3390/antibiotics15070661). MEGARes acquired-gene groups are the wrong instrument for this organism; the point_mutation class is suppressed by design.

Candida auris.note: WHO fungal priority pathogen, critical group. Species identification alone warrants culture; MEGARes does not cover antifungals, so no escalating class applies.

Candida albicans.note: WHO fungal priority pathogen, critical group. No antifungal coverage in MEGARes.

Candida haemulonii.note: C. auris near-neighbour in the C. haemulonii complex; misidentification between them is well documented, so the call is worth a look on its own.

Mycobacterium abscessus.note: Rapidly growing non-tuberculous mycobacterium, difficult to treat.
